description: Building a harmonized wildfire hotspot calendar that merges MODIS and VIIRS into one consistent record from 2002 to today, with stated uncertainty and held-out validation. React map app: draw an area, see fire history, anomalies, current month vs historical median, and download CSVs.
summary:
Fire Harmonize puts NASA FIRMS MODIS and VIIRS active-fire detections on one consistent monthly record and shows it as a burning-activity calendar for any area a user chooses inside a processed region.

MODIS Aqua (from 2002) has the long history; VIIRS (from 2012) sees smaller fires, so it counts more. Adding them creates a false jump in 2012. We convert MODIS to a VIIRS-equivalent scale with a model fitted on the years both sensors flew and tested by leaving each year out. Every value has a source flag (viirs_native, modis_estimated, provisional) and every estimate a range; nothing is shown as exact. A typical estimated month is off by about 18% in Zambia, within our 30% target, and 42% in Western North America, above it and flagged in the app.

Users draw an area or enter coordinates and see a 2002 to 2026 month-by-year calendar, the busiest months and years (with how sure we are), the fire season and whether it is shifting, anomalies, and how the latest month compares with normal. They can compare two areas, listen to the calendar, and download CSV files and a PDF report per region. A static web app for emergency responders, land managers and scientists. Demo regions: Western North America and Zambia.
details:
Live app: https://fireharmonize.vercel.app
Code: https://github.com/Yasaswini-ch/Fire-harmonize

Slide Deck : https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1lSr4f2py1R5LyWsd56sRx0SGCetpuPsE/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=115912266138453067043&rtpof=true&sd=true

What it does

Satellites have recorded active fires since 2000, but across two sensor families. MODIS (1 km pixels) has the long record; VIIRS (375 m pixels, from 2012) detects smaller fires and therefore counts more. Simply adding them produces a false jump in 2012. Fire Harmonize converts the MODIS record to a VIIRS-equivalent monthly scale, attaches an uncertainty range to every estimated number, and presents the result as an interactive burning-activity calendar.

How it works

  1. Data: NASA FIRMS standard-processing archive (MODIS Aqua, VIIRS Suomi NPP, VIIRS NOAA-20), the FIRMS area API for the current year, and near-real-time NOAA-20 for the latest months (marked provisional).
  2. Filters: only detections typed as presumed vegetation fire, Aqua only, low-confidence detections dropped, static sources such as gas flares removed with a location mask.
  3. Grid: detections are summed into 0.25 degree cells by calendar month.
  4. Harmonization: MODIS counts before VIIRS existed are converted to VIIRS-equivalent with a ratio fitted per calendar month and level of MODIS activity on the 2012-2021 overlap. Five candidate models were compared by leaving each year out in turn.
  5. Uncertainty: each estimated month carries a 10th-90th percentile range from held-out years, set separately for areas of 1-2, 2-3 and 3-5 degrees and for the whole region. These are empirical ranges, not formal confidence intervals.
  6. Continuity: NOAA-20 is checked against Suomi NPP rather than assumed equal.

Every value carries a source flag: viirs_native, modis_estimated or provisional. The harmonization is never presented as exact.

What the app shows

  • A month-by-year calendar (2002-2026) with estimated months hatched
  • Busiest months and years, fire season, and annual anomalies
  • "Now vs normal": the latest month against the median of the same calendar month
  • A map and 3D globe of detections
  • A compare-two-areas view
  • Plain-language results and a guide to every graph
  • CSV downloads, chart images and a PDF report
  • A calendar you can listen to, a guided walkthrough, and shareable links

Users can draw any area inside a processed region. Adding a region is one entry in a config file.

How we tested it (leave-one-year-out, 2012-2021)

  • Western North America: typical error of an estimated month is 9% for the whole region, 39% (3-5 degrees), 58% (2-3 degrees) and 99% (1-2 degrees, where there are very few detections per month).
  • Zambia: 10% for the whole region, and 17%, 18% and 20% for the same area sizes.
  • Bias across sample areas: -0.8% and 0.0%. Ranges cover held-out months 76-81% of the time against an 80% target.
  • The static-source mask was tested on 84 months: it removes 92% of static sources in Western North America and 82% in Zambia, and wrongly removes 0.30% and 0.03% of vegetation fires.
  • The August 2026 near-real-time month in Zambia, the largest on record, was cross-checked with Suomi NPP and MODIS and found to be real.

The app shows all of this under "Accuracy and methods".

Benefits and impact

Emergency responders and land managers can see at once whether the latest month is unusual for a place and how far to trust each number. Scientists get a consistent record with its uncertainty stated. Accuracy is solid at region scale, with wider uncertainty for small areas, and the app says so.

Limitations (stated in the app)

  • The MODIS-to-VIIRS relationship is fitted on 2012-2021 and assumed for 2002-2011, which cannot be checked.
  • Counts are detections, not area burned. The time step is monthly. Recent months are provisional.
  • The PDF report covers whole regions only.

Tools

Python 3.11 (pandas, NumPy, pyarrow, matplotlib, requests, ReportLab) for the data pipeline. React, Vite, Leaflet, Recharts, d3-scale-chromatic, three.js and topojson-client for the static web app. Deployed on Vercel.

What is creative

Honesty about uncertainty is the core feature: ranges and source flags on every estimate, error reported by area size, a calendar that marks estimated months without relying on colour alone, colour-blind-safe scales, a keyboard-navigable calendar, and an audible version of the calendar.

Use of Super Intelligence

An AI coding assistant (Claude Code, by Anthropic) was used under the author's direction to help write parts of the data pipeline, the web application, the tests and the documentation. All figures in the app are computed by the pipeline from NASA FIRMS data and its validation, not generated by the assistant.
dataRefs: NASA FIRMS (Fire Information for Resource Management System)
FIRMS Active Fire Data: MODIS Collection 6.1 and VIIRS 375 m (Suomi NPP, NOAA-20)
NASA Visible Earth: Blue Marble (opening-page globe)
NASA SVS: Deep Star Maps (opening-page star field)
